title: The b3 French
description: Fight the French with the Papa-Ticulat Gambit. This opening pairs best with the b3 Sicilian.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1b1pp/4p3/5pP1/3np1n1/1PN3Q1.text:
Black plays the only move, f7-f5!

We'll attack Black's knight once more with h2-h3.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2n1p3/3n2P1/4p2P/1PN5/.text:
We'll support the g-pawn with h2-h4. White now has a slight objective edge and great attacking prospects on the kingside.

We will look to recapture the d-pawn with our queen, and our f1-bishop can (but doesn't have to) develop to g2.

In all of these b3 French positions, any Nxc3 should be met with dxc3.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2n1p3/3n2P1/4p3/1PN5/P.text: Black jumps the knight into d5, opening up an attack on the g-pawn.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/2n1pn2/8/4p1P1/1PN5/PB.text:
Black develops the queenside knight to c6 - this is the most common.

We'll attack Black's knight by pushing the g-pawn up to g5!

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4p3/6P1/3np1n1/1PN1Q3/.text:
Black attacks our queen once again by jumping their knight into g4.

Our queen needs to keep an eye on f2, so we'll move it to g3 and attack the marauding knight.

r1bq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4pn2/6P1/3np3/1PN5/PBP.text:
Black counterattacks our queen by jumping their knight into d4. This is the critical move, and the crazy ensuing sequence of moves is forced.

We'll slide our queen up to e3.

r1bq1rk1/ppp3p1/3bp2p/5pP1/6PQ/1P3N2/PBP.text:
We develop our knight to f3. This move might seem a little slow, but we need to prevent Qxg5. The computer only gives a slight edge for White, but this position is incredibly difficult to defend from a human standpoint.

We're down an exchange, but we have a raging kingside attack and two of Black's pieces aren't even playing. One of our main motifs is Bxg7!

r1bq1rk1/ppp3p1/3bp2p/5pP1/6PQ/1P6/PBPP4.text: Black prevents Qxh7+ with h7-h6. This is, once again, the only move that doesn't lose.

r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/3bp3/5pP1/3n2n1/1PN2pQP/.text:
Black captures en passant and opens up an attack on our queen.

We'll move our queen out to h4. The g4-knight is still under attack and Black can't simply move it since the d4-knight would then be en prise.

r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/3bp3/5pP1/3np1n1/1PN3QP/.text:
Black counterattacks our queen by moving their bishop to d6.

We'll block the attack with f2-f4!

r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/3bp3/5pP1/6PQ/1P6/PBPP4/.text:
Black captures our rook on d1 and makes a queen with check!

We'll recapture on d1 - this is the only legal move.

r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/3bp3/5pP1/6nQ/1P5P/PBPPp.text:
Black recaptures on e2 with the pawn.

We'll capture on g4 - threatening the devastating Qxh7+!

r1bq1rk1/ppp3pp/3bp3/5pP1/6nQ/1PN2p1P/PB.text:
So Black jumps the knight into e2 and gives a check to our king! This is the only move that doesn't lose material.

We'll capture on e2 with our c-knight. This is important since we want to open the long diagonal for our b2-bishop.

rn1q1rk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/4p1P1/4p1b1/1PN5/P.text:
Black counterattacks our queen by developing the bishop to g4.

Our rook and queen are skewered, so we will have to interpose with f2-f3.

rn1q1rk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/4p1P1/6b1/1PN2p2/P.text:
Black captures on f3.

We'll recapture with the knight.

rn1q1rk1/ppp1bppp/8/3np1P1/6b1/1PN2N2/PB.text:
Black's knight was under attack, so they jump it into d5.

If Black had tried pushing e4 instead, we would simply win material by capturing on f6.
We attack Black's bishop with Rg1. With the more active pieces, and with great attacking prospects on the kingside, White is now simply better.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4p3/3n2P1/4p2P/1PN5/PKP.text:
We support the g-pawn with h2-h4. The position is now close to equality, but White certainly has an easier game and great attacking prospects in the middlegame.

We should look to capture the e-pawn (preferably with our queen), and the f1-bishop can develop to g2.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4p3/3n2P1/4p3/1PN5/PKPP.text: Black jumps the knight into d5, opening up an attack on the g-pawn.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4pn2/6P1/4p3/1PN5/PbPPQ.text:
Black trades bishops on b2.

We'll recapture.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4pn2/8/1b2p3/1PN5/PBPPQ.text:
Black moves the queen over to e7 and is looking to follow up with Ba3.

We'll push g2-g4 and are looking to dislodge Black's knight by pushing the pawn up to g5.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4pn2/8/4p1P1/1PP5/PBP1Q.text:
We kickstart an attack on the kingside with g2-g4! White now has a slight objective edge, and great attacking prospects in the middlegame.

We can look to dislodge Black's knight with g5, and support g5 with h2-h4. We should also look to open up our dark-squared bishop with c4, and our f1-bishop can develop to g2.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4pn2/8/4p1P1/bPN5/PBPPQ.text:
Black follows up with Ba3. The main idea is to trade the dark-squared bishops and weaken the dark squares around our king.

We'll attack Black's knight by pushing the g-pawn up to g5.

rnb1k2r/ppp1qppp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PP5/PBP1QPP.text: Black slides the queen over to e7.

rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PN5/PBPPQP.text:
Black castles kingside.

We still don't take on e4! Instead, we'll kickstart a kingside attack with g2-g4 and are looking to dislodge Black's knight by pushing the pawn up to g5.

A useful rule of thumb is that, in all of these positions, a7-a5 should be met with a2-a4.

rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/5n2/4p3/4p1P1/1PN5/PBP.text:
Black pushes e5 and opens up an attack on the g4-pawn.

We'll attack Black's knight by pushing the g-pawn up to g5! Black now has two options...

rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/8/3np1P1/4p2P/1PN5/PBP.text:
We support the g-pawn with h2-h4. White now has a comfortable edge and great attacking prospects on the kingside.

We should look to capture the e-pawn (preferably with our queen), and our bishop can offer to trade itself on h3.

rnbq1rk1/ppp1bppp/8/3np1P1/4p3/1PN5/PBPP.text: Black jumps the knight into d5, opening up an attack on the g-pawn.

rnbqk2r/ppp1bppp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PN5/PBPPQPP.text:
The most common is 5...Be7 - Black develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares to castle kingside.

Don't rush to recapture! We should proceed by castling queenside.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/1b2p3/1PN5/PBPPQP.text:
Black develops the bishop to b4. The main idea of this move is to prevent us from recapturing the pawn on e4.

We'll proceed by castling queenside.

If Black replies by castling kingside, we should simply recapture on e4.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/4p3/1Pb5/PBPPQPPP.text:
Our knight was attacking the e-pawn, so Black chooses to remove it by capturing on c3.

We'll recapture with the d-pawn, opening up the d-file for our rook.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PN5/PBPP1PP.text:
Black defends the e-pawn by developing the kingside knight to f6.

We move our queen over to e2 and add an attacker to to the e-pawn. Black now has options...

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/4P3/1P6/P1PP1PP.text:
Black follows up on their previous move by advancing the d-pawn and challenging our central pawn.

We'll fianchetto our bishop, offering up the e-pawn for capture! Black can now accept the gambit or decline it in a variety of ways...

The move c7-c5 would now transpose to the b3 Sicilian with 2...e6 - refer to the course on the b3 Sicilian!

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/4p3/1P6/PBPP1PPP/.text:
Black challenges the authority of our gambit by capturing the e4-pawn.

We'll develop our queenside knight and attack the e4-pawn. Our plan is Nc3/Qe2/0-0-0/g4, in various orders.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
Black replies with 1...e6 - this is the third most popular response to 1. e4.

The idea is quite simple - the move e7-e6 supports the advance d7-d5.

We'll go for an interesting sideline with b2-b3. 

French players are often well-prepared in the main lines - in this sideline we hope either:

(1) They think we're terrible and take the pawn/hope for the best.

(2) They get too scared of our gambit and play too passively.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
Welcome to the b3 French! 

In this study, we will learn how to handle the position which arises after Black accepts our gambit and defends the e-pawn with their kingside knight. More precisely, this study will be dealing with Black's continuations 5...Be7 and 5...Bb4.

We'll open with 1.e4.

rnb1kb1r/ppp3pp/4p3/5p2/4n3/1PN5/PBP2PPP.text:
Black captures on e4 with the knight.

We'll capture Black's knight on e4.

rnb1kb1r/ppp3pp/4p3/8/3Rp3/1P6/PBP2PPP/4.text: We continue Rd4, looking to capture the e-pawn. White now has a pleasant edge and (after Rxe4) can continue with Bd3/Bb5, Nf3 and O-O.

rnb1kb1r/ppp3pp/4pn2/5p2/4P3/1PN5/PBP2PP.text:
Black trades the queens.

We'll recapture with the rook.

rnb1kb1r/ppp3pp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PN4N/PBP2PPP.text:
We continue Nh3, looking to jump our knight into g5 or f4! The evaluation of this position is close to equality, but White retains great practical chances with the superior piece activity and Black's weak pawns on the e-file.

We will look to continue with Ng5/Nf4, Bc4 and O-O.

rnb1kb1r/ppp3pp/4pn2/8/4p3/1PN5/PBP2PPP/.text: Black captures on e4 with the f-pawn.

rnbqkb1r/ppp3pp/4pn2/5p2/4p3/1PNP4/PBP2P.text:
Black doesn't capture on d3 and instead develops the kingside knight.

We'll proceed by capturing on e4.

rnbqkb1r/ppp3pp/4pn2/5p2/8/1PNB4/PBP1QPP.text:
We move our queen to e2, pinning the e6-pawn and preparing O-O-O. White objectively better, and the position is very pleasant. 

The immediate threat is Bxf5, and Black will struggle to defend against the pressure which will be built up with Nf3, O-O-O & Bc4.

We should look to meet Bb4 with a3.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/4P3/1P6/P1PP1PP.text:
Black follows up on their previous move by advancing the d-pawn and challenging our central pawn.

We fianchetto our bishop, offering up the e-pawn for capture! Black can now accept the gambit or decline it in a variety of ways...

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/4p3/1P6/PBPP1PPP/.text:
Black challenges the authority of our gambit by capturing the e4-pawn.

We'll develop our queenside knight and attack the e4-pawn. Our plan is Nc3/Qe2/0-0-0/g4, in various orders.

rnbqkbnr/ppp3pp/4p3/5p2/4p3/1PN5/PBPP1PP.text:
Black supports the e-pawn with f7-f5.

We push d2-d3, looking to chip away at Black's central structure.

rnbqkbnr/ppp3pp/4p3/5p2/8/1PNp4/PBP2PPP/.text:
Black captures on d3.

We'll recapture with the bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The French Defense.

We will fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
We're continuing our analysis of the French Defense with 2.b3. 

In this study, we will learn how to handle the position which arises after Black accepts our gambit and supports the e-pawn with their f-pawn.

We'll open with e4.

lessons.title: Black Declines With 3...Nf6 and 3...d4
lessons.chapter: Black Doesn't Play Into The Gambit

r1bqk2r/1p1n1pbp/p1n1p1p1/2ppP3/P4PQ1/1P.text:
We continue a2-a4, preventing Black from easily expanding with b7-b5. White now has a slight edge, and we will look to proceed by castling short.

The arising middlegame is very rich. Some typical ideas include h2-h4 and the maneuver Nd1-Ne3/Nf2.

r1bqk2r/pp1n1pbp/2n1p1p1/2ppP3/5PQ1/1P3N.text:
Black fianchettoes their bishop.

We develop the queenside knight. We are now looking to jump the knight into b5, from where it will be able to access the d6 outpost.

The move d4 is never an issue, since it gives us the important e4 square.

r1bqkb1r/pp1n1p1p/2n1p1p1/2ppP3/5PQ1/1P3.text:
Black plays g7-g6, preparing to fianchetto the f8-bishop.

We'll prepare to castle kingside by developing the f1-bishop to e2.

If Black now attacks our queen with h2-h4, we should retreat it to g3.

r1bqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/2n1p3/2ppP3/5PQ1/1P6/P.text:
Black develops the queenside knight.

We'll develop the kingside knight. Black can continue in a variety of ways, but our general plan is Be2 and O-O.

r1bqkbnr/p4ppp/2p1p3/2p5/4P3/1PP2N2/PB3P.text: We recapture on c3 with the d-pawn. White is now simply better - we have a lead in development, a great bishop on b2, and Black's queenside pawn structure is damaged beyond repair.

r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/1Bp5/4P3/1Pp2N2/PB.text:
Black attempts to solve their problems by capturing on c3 and releasing the tension.

We'll capture on c6, forcing Black to double their c-pawns!

r1bqkbnr/pp3ppp/2n1p3/2p5/3pP3/1PP2N2/PB.text:
Black develops the queenside knight and further supports the d4-pawn.

5...dxc3 would merely leave us with a big lead in development after 6.Nxc3.

After 5...Nc6, we'll develop our light-squared bishop on b5, pinning the knight. Not only are we threatening to win a pawn with cxd4, but we also threaten to double Black's c-pawns with Bxc6.

r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/2n1pn2/1B6/3pP3/1P3N2/P.text:
Black recaptures on d4.

We capture on d4 with the knight.

r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/2n1pn2/1Bp5/3pP3/1PP2N2.text:
Black develops the kingside knight.

We'll capture the pawn on d4.

r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/4pn2/1B6/3BP3/1P6/P2PQP.text:
We capture Black's knight on d4. The idea of Qe2 is now apparent - if our queen wasn't on e2, Black would have been able to capture the b5-bishop!

White now simply has an extra pawn, and should look to continue with O-O.

r2qkb1r/pp1b1ppp/4pn2/1B6/3nP3/1P6/PB1PQ.text: Black captures our knight on d4.

r2qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/2n1p3/1Bp5/3pP3/1PP2N2/.text:
Black supports and unpins the knight by moving their bishop to d7.

We'll move our queen to e2. This move might not make too much sense at first glance, but it is important that we support the bishop on b5.

r2qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/2n1p3/1Bp5/4P3/1PP2N2/P.text:
We recapture on c3 with the d-pawn. This is probably the best Black can get, but White still has an edge and White's position is easier to play.

We'll continue with Nbd2 and O-O.

r2qkbnr/pp1b1ppp/2n1p3/1Bp5/4P3/1Pp2N2/P.text: Black captures the pawn on c3.

rnbqkb1r/pp1n1ppp/4p3/2ppP3/6Q1/1P6/PBPP.text:
Black continues in typical French style by pushing the c-pawn and taking some central space.

We'll push f2-f4, supporting the e5 pawn and preparing to develop the g1-knight behind the f-pawn.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p3/2npP3/8/1P1P4/PBP2P.text:
Black jumps the knight to c5.

We'll push d4 and attack Black's knight once more!

If Black now jumps the knight back to e4, we should play for g3 and f3. It is important to play g3 before f3 in order to prevent Black from playing Qh4+.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4p3/3pP3/4n3/1P6/PBPP1P.text:
Black might also jump the knight into e4, but this isn't great since the knight simply becomes a target.

We'll attack Black's knight with d2-d3!

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p4/4P3/1P6/PBPP1P.text:
Black declines the gambit by developing the kingside knight.

We'll push forward and attack Black's knight on f6!

rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P4/1P1B4/PBP.text:
We develop our bishop to d3. Black moved the same piece four times in the opening - White now simply has a space advantage and a huge lead in development. 

We should look to continue developing with c2-c3, Nge2 and O-O.

rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/3P4/1P6/PBP2P.text: Black retreats the knight to d7.

rnbqkb1r/pppn1ppp/4p3/3pP3/8/1P6/PBPP1PP.text:
Black retreats the knight to d7.

We'll proceed by developing our queen out to g4. 

We place the queen there to limit the movement of Black's dark-squared bishop. Black is generally forced to eventually play g7-g6. 

Then our idea is to get the queen out of the way and advance the g- and h- pawns.

rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/4p3/2p5/3pP3/1P3N2/PBPP1.text:
Black supports the d-pawn with c7-c5.

Instead, 4...Nc6 would allow us to play 5.Bb5 and win the d4-pawn.

We'll push c2-c3, creating tension between the pawns and threatening to capture the pawn on d4.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/3p4/4P3/1P6/P1PP1PP.text:
Black follows up on their previous move by advancing the d-pawn and challenging our central pawn.

We fianchetto our bishop, offering up the e-pawn for capture! We are going to look at a couple of ways of declining the gambit.

rnbqkbnr/ppp2ppp/4p3/8/3pP3/1P6/PBPP1PPP.text:
Black declines the gambit by pushing the d-pawn to d4. This is not a great move, since we can target the pawn.

We'll develop our kingside knight and attack Black's d-pawn.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
Black plays the French Defense.

We will go for our fianchetto idea.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In this chapter, we're going to learn how to respond if Black decides to decline our gambit with Nf6 or d4.

We'll begin with 1.e4.

r2qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1pn1p3/8/3QP3/1PN5/PBP2.text: Black develops their queenside knight and attacks our queen.

r2qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1pn1p3/8/4P3/1PN5/PBPQ1.text:
We retreat the queen to e2. White now has a slight edge and great attacking prospects on the kingside. 

We'll look to continue with O-O-O, Nge2 and f2-f3, and we can launch a kingside attack with h2-h4 and g2-g4.

r3k1n1/pbpp1p2/np2p1p1/1N5r/1b2P3/1PB5/P.text:
We retreat the bishop to c3 - this is the only move that keeps the extra pawn! We should look to continue by supporting the e-pawn with f2-f3 as soon as possible.

Notable is that we can simply meet Bxe4 with Bxb4 and Nxc7+.

r3k1n1/pbpp1pB1/np2p1p1/1N5r/1b2P3/1P6/P.text: Black moves the rook up to h5.

r3k1nr/pbpp1pp1/np2p1p1/1N6/1b2P3/1P6/PB.text:
Black defends the c7 square by moving the knight out to a6.

But now we can capture the pawn on g7!

rn1qk1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/1b2P3/1PN5/PBP.text:
Black develops the bishop out to b4. The idea of this move is to remove the only defender of the e4-pawn.

We'll move our queen out to g4 and attack the g7-pawn!

rn1qk1r1/pbpp1p1Q/1p2pn2/8/1b6/1PN5/PBPP.text:
Black defends the rook and attacks our queen by retreating their knight to f6.

We slide our queen back to h4 and attack Black's bishop on b4.

rn1qk1r1/pbpp1p1p/1p2p2Q/8/1b2n3/1PN5/PB.text:
Black captures the pawn on e4.

We'll capture the pawn on h7 and attack Black's rook.

rn1qk1r1/pbpp1pQp/1p2pn2/8/1b2P3/1PN5/PB.text:
Black moves the rook to g8 and attacks our queen.

We'll move our queen to the only safe square, h6.

If Black now proceeds with Rg6, we can simply retreat the queen to e3 and defend our e4-pawn.

rn1qk1r1/pbppbp2/1p2pn2/8/7Q/1PN5/PBPP1P.text:
We proceed by castling queenside. 

The immediate Ng4 should now be met with Qh7, and we can meet a subsequent Nf6 with Qh3, holding onto g2.

We are a pawn up, and the onus is on Black to demonstrate that they have any compensation.
Black retreats the bishop to e7.

rn1qk2r/p1ppbppp/1p2p3/3bP3/3P4/1P5N/PBP.text:
We develop our knight out to h3 and are looking to jump it into f4. White now has a comfortable objective edge and great attacking prospects on the kingside.

We'll continue with Nf4 & Bd3, and can try to get Qg4 and O-O-O.

rn1qk2r/p1ppbppp/1p2p3/3bP3/3P4/1P6/PBP2.text: Black develops their dark-squared bishop, preparing O-O.

rn1qk2r/pbp1bppp/1p3n2/3p4/6P1/1PN2Q2/PB.text: Out of nowhere, we launch a kingside attack with g4! White now has a very comfortable edge with great attacking prospects on the kingside.

rn1qk2r/pbp1bppp/1p3n2/3p4/8/1PN2Q2/PBPP.text: Black develops the dark-squared bishop, preparing O-O.

rn1qk2r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/1b2P1Q1/1PN5/P.text:
Black develops the knight and attacks our queen. This move gives up the g7 pawn, but it is the engine's top choice.

We'll capture the pawn on g7.

rn1qkb1r/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/3bP3/8/1P6/PBPP1.text:
Black recaptures with the bishop.

We'll push d4, expanding in the center and supporting the e5-pawn.

If Black now tries to undermine our pawns with ...c5, we should expand further with c4 and d5!

rn1qkb1r/pbp2ppp/1p3n2/3p4/8/1PN2Q2/PBPP.text:
Black develops the kingside knight.

We'll proceed by castling queenside.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/3nP3/8/1PN5/PBPP.text:
Black jumps the knight into d5.

We'll exchange it off.

rn1qkb1r/pbpp1ppp/1p2pn2/8/4P3/1PN5/PBPP.text:
Black develops the kingside knight and adds an attacker to the e4-pawn.

We'll push e5 and attack Black's knight!

rn1qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1p2p3/2p5/4P3/1PN5/PBP.text:
Black pushes c7-c5, turning the position into an unusual Sicilian.

We'll strike in the center by pushing our d-pawn two squares.

rn1qkbnr/pb1p1ppp/1p2p3/8/3pP3/1PN5/PBP2.text:
Black captures on d4.

We recapture on d4 with the queen.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p2p3/3p4/4P3/1PN5/PBPP.text:
Black strikes in the center with d5.

We'll respond by capturing the d-pawn.

rn1qkbnr/pbp2ppp/1p6/3p4/8/1PN5/PBPP1PPP.text:
Black recaptures.

We'll prepare to castle queenside by developing our queen on f3.

rn1qkbnr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p3/8/4P3/1P6/PBPP1P.text:
Black fianchettoes their bishop and attacks our e4-pawn.

We'll defend the e-pawn by developing the queenside knight to c3. 

After this we have to consider a few handful of options for Black.

rn2k1nr/pbpp1pp1/1p2p1p1/8/1b2P3/1PN5/PB.text:
Black recaptures on g6, opening the h-file for their rook.

We'll jump our knight into b5. This move threatens Nxc7+ and opens up an attack on the g7-pawn!

rn2k1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2p1q1/8/1b2P1Q1/1PN5/.text:
Black slides the queen over to g6 and offers a queen trade.

We'll oblige and trade queens on g6.

rn2k1nr/pbpp1ppp/1p2pq2/8/1b2P1Q1/1PN5/P.text:
Black moves the queen out to f6 and defends the g-pawn - this is the most natural and most common move here.

We'll proceed by castling queenside. We are now threatening to win on the spot with the crushing Nd5!

If Black now attacks our queen with Nh6, we should retreat it to e2.

rnbqkbnr/p1pp1ppp/1p2p3/8/4P3/1P6/P1PP1P.text:
Black chooses not to advance with d5, and instead sets up with e6 and b6.

We'll simply fianchetto our bishop.

rnbqkbnr/pppp1ppp/4p3/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
The start of the French Defense.

We'll go for our fianchetto!

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
We're concluding our analysis of the French Defense with 2.b3. In this study, we will learn how to play the position if Black chooses to play with b7-b6 instead of d7-d5.

Let's begin, as before, with 1.e4.
